scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported polygon covers 1492 to 1500 in northern Tocantins, consistent with this people’s broad regional identity. It is not a verified precolonial boundary or the modern demarcated land.
Apinayé and Apinajé are spelling variants here; Canela Apanyekrá, Krahô, Xerente and other Timbira peoples remain distinct. No shared card association is proposed.
The 1970, 1979 and 1991 dates are museum collection entries, not manufacture dates. Catalogue descriptions were read; object photographs were not independently analyzed.
An outdated ethnic-language note transcribed from a 1973 museum file is not used. The current catalogue attribution is distinguished from that legacy classification.

The 2020 music study was read in full-text excerpts. Interview testimony is attributed; concerns about future transmission are not evidence of disappearance or a uniform lack of interest among young people.

The seed statement is a dated community account, not a current crop census. The nursery report labels outputs as realized but provides conflicting project durations; no precise completion year is asserted.
The 1997 original decree verifies homologation separately from the 1985 declaration and demarcation. No claim is made that it resolved all excluded-land claims.
No verified conquest or single successor is appropriate. Independent historical review, polygon review and depth certification remain pending.
